why: A window of k points is strictly increasing exactly when its k - 1 adjacent steps all go up. Track the length of the current strictly increasing run as you slide; the window ending at i is valid whenever that run is at least k long.
hints: Checking every window from scratch costs O(n k). What can you carry from position i - 1 to position i?
Keep run = length of the strictly increasing streak ending at i (reset to 1 when y[i-1] >= y[i]). The window of size k ending at i is valid exactly when run >= k.
One pass, add 1 whenever run >= k. O(n) time, O(1) space; k = 1 counts every point.
pitfalls: Equal neighbours break the streak: strictly increasing means <, not <=.
Overlapping windows count separately: [1,2,3,4] with k = 3 gives 2.
k = 1: every single point is a valid window.
